scope_and_independence.compilation_coverage: Reviewed global29-entry manifest:28 actual executed targets plus one inspected non-executable HA ADR. Earlier074/075/082 checks are retained, not relabeled as new execution.
scope_and_independence.honest_boundary: A distinct skeptical developer lens, not an external human endorsement or an assertion of independent authorship for own 16 chapters. Prior substantive reading/authoring and independent reviews are retained; this final pass does not claim a fresh line-by-line prose reread of every chapter.

adversarial_scenarios.scenario: Put two default servers behind one load balancer and interpret readiness as shared durable state.
adversarial_scenarios.observed: The actual fresh-process record loses service/task/node/custom-namespace records while the same manually associated owned container remains running. A separate ready process is not a shared state owner.
adversarial_scenarios.reason: Chapter34 explicitly rejects two memory servers as HA; Chapter09 requires a new durable composition, not a constructor substitution.
adversarial_scenarios.scope: Two simultaneously load-balanced servers were not executed. Their independent maps follow inspected constructors; the actual restart experiment is deliberately manual container association, not agent adoption.

adversarial_scenarios.scenario: Use one successful task CAS to claim that two schedulers cannot overcommit different tasks or host ports.
adversarial_scenarios.observed: The separate full sixteen-schema fixture has exactly one winner and one conflict for one pending task. SQL predicates task ID/UpdatedAt/pending state; row_version is incremented but not the compared guard.
adversarial_scenarios.reason: Both chapters explicitly distinguish per-task ownership from cross-row CPU/port reservation and warn that ordinary immediate placement bypasses Plan. Worked answers identify the same predicates and limitation.
adversarial_scenarios.scope: No global reservation implementation or live two-planner overcommit experiment was invented; the broader race is source-derived analysis.

adversarial_scenarios.scenario: Partition a worker, reschedule its stateless task, and infer that the old container has stopped.
adversarial_scenarios.observed: Returned-node deterministic tests exercise owned cleanup. Desired-stopped/removed objects leave active accounting before a physical daemon acknowledgement.
adversarial_scenarios.reason: Chapter19/37 distinguish server authority from host reality and eventual cleanup from fencing; stateful work and local volumes are kept separate.
adversarial_scenarios.scope: No real network partition or simultaneous request-serving overlap was executed by this review. Fake cleanup is not network or disk fencing.

adversarial_scenarios.scenario: Accept 250m/128Mi and cite direct Docker adapter support as proof that the ordinary agent enforces limits.
adversarial_scenarios.observed: Actual ordinary handler→Runner→Docker HostConfig was Memory=0/NanoCPUs=0; the direct adapter received Memory=134217728/NanoCPUs=250000000.
adversarial_scenarios.reason: The book traces both missing data boundaries rather than assigning planner or direct-adapter guarantees to ordinary deployment. Requested accounting is distinguished from runtime measurement.
adversarial_scenarios.scope: Cached-image/owned-ID teaching guards and no host-published workload ports are recorded; no production-kernel isolation certification.

adversarial_scenarios.scenario: Restart during rollout or report deployment success and infer fresh-process persistence and physical stop completion.
adversarial_scenarios.observed: The chaos case constructs a new controller over the same retained MemoryService. Actual bounded rollout reaches succeeded with pending_stops=1.
adversarial_scenarios.reason: Final Chapter 17 now explicitly says the next pass uses desired/store accounting before physical acknowledgement. Chapter37 names the retained-store test and separate fresh-process experiment.
adversarial_scenarios.scope: The earlier overstatement was corrected before final formats and is independently visible in current text. No restart-during-real-production-rollout experiment claimed.

adversarial_scenarios.scenario: Make the second sorted GitOps manifest invalid and assume a failed sync means the first service is unchanged.
adversarial_scenarios.reason: Chapter30 walks exactly this failure: first mutation remains, LastError changes and LastRevision can still be the prior successful revision. The actual fresh Lab07 partial-apply assertion passed. Prune is explicitly a previous-name set, not a current stable ownership predicate.
adversarial_scenarios.scope: Real local Git/in-process application methods; no external repository, daemon workload or repository-wide transaction.

adversarial_scenarios.scenario: Cancel an advisory-lock lease, observe Done closed, and immediately allow a successor to assume the database lock and all old effects are gone.

observed.scope: package cancellation path with healthy pooled session, not running server HA

adversarial_scenarios.reason: Chapter34 explains pooled connection release versus session unlock and the Done-closed fast path. Cooperative callback cancellation, in-flight effects and absent default leadership wiring remain separate.
adversarial_scenarios.scope: Observed package behavior on the owned PostgreSQL fixture; not a running replicated server or physical workload fencing demonstration.

adversarial_scenarios.scenario: Treat the baseline 447 passes as evidence that the guarded database suite passed, then silently repair its fixture to get green results.

observed.original_postgres_fixture: Two failures SQLSTATE42703, one rollback test passes; fixture applies1–14, agent_version added16.

adversarial_scenarios.reason: The final narrative and gate retain all skips and original database failures; separate full-schema teaching execution never overwrites that baseline.
adversarial_scenarios.scope: This final review inspected existing raw records; it did not rerun destructive database tests or relabel their outcomes.

resolved_prior_findings.finding: An earlier sentence implied physical-stop acknowledgement before capacity reuse. Final text explicitly describes desired/store accounting; actual rollout has succeeded with pending_stops=1.
resolved_prior_findings.revalidation: Final canonical chapter inspected; source IsActiveTask and actual rollout timeline agree. Root final export/text/raster gates bind the corrected content to final artifacts.

reader_usability.assessment: The source-guided explanations and worked answers identify concrete state owners, predicates, failure windows and observable outcomes. Exact listings have pinned context; original extensions retain module-relative setup. The reader can distinguish expected procedures from actual output.
reader_usability.practical_followability: examples/README.md explains fragments versus complete programs and internal-package module placement. REPRODUCE.md states that sourceZIP excludes the application/site snapshots, requires retrieving the pinned application separately, and is not a standalone Jekyll checkout.
remaining_limits: Short code fragments are not individually compilable empty-module examples; full containing packages/registered overlays provide setup.
Some optional Docker/Compose/network procedures remain expected-only; precise actual harness modes are stated.
The final PDF is content/raster equivalent across routine rebuilds, not promised byte-deterministic.

GitOps filesystem path checking is lexical; hostile symlink sandboxing remains a source-derived unresolved threat-model question in CAP-019, not an executed exploit or guaranteed filesystem confinement.
